ENT CLINICAL NOTE  

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure: New-onset left-sided throbbing headache since waking the previous morning; no clear precipitating exposure identified (possible work-related stress).
- Symptom timeline and progression: Continuous baseline pain for ≈24 h with intermittent worsening; photophobia; alleviated when lying in a dark room. No sudden thunderclap onset.
- ENT symptoms: Denies throat swelling/closure sensation, voice change, dysphagia/odynophagia, drooling, nasal/ocular discharge beyond photophobia, stridor/noisy breathing, dyspnea, facial/lip/tongue/uvular swelling, ear pain/hearing changes, neck pain/swelling.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments: No prior similar headaches or ENT-related episodes. Took paracetamol with partial relief; has avoided aspirin/NSAIDs because of aspirin allergy.
- Allergies and current medications:  
  • Allergy – Aspirin → nausea (patient-reported).  
  • Medications – Microgynon (combined OCP) daily (exact dose/strength not documented); Paracetamol 1 g up to TID PRN (exact dose/frequency not fully documented).
- Social context: Lives with friends/housemates; currently at home.

Objective:
- Observable swelling: None stated.
- Airway/breathing: No stridor, dyspnea, or voice change reported.
- Mental status: Alert, coherent during call; no dizziness or syncope.
- Vitals / physical examination: Not recorded (telephone consultation).
- Accompaniment: Not specified during call.

Assessment:
- Working impression: New-onset unilateral throbbing headache most consistent with migraine without aura.
  • Evidence: Left-sided throbbing pain, photophobia, relief in dark, female in 30s, positive family history of migraine, no focal neurology, no systemic illness.
- Differential diagnosis (from DDx, aligned with transcript):
  1. Migraine without aura – high likelihood; see above supporting features. Opposing: lacks nausea/vomiting; first episode at age 31.
  2. Tension-type/stress-related headache – moderate likelihood; work stress and fluctuating pain support; opposing: unilateral throbbing and photophobia less typical.
  3. Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis – low-moderate; risk factor (combined OCP) and new headache; opposing: no focal deficits, rapid onset <24 h, no papilledema or seizure.  
- No ENT or airway compromise noted.

Plan:
- Immediate actions/advice:
  • Start an NSAID (e.g., ibuprofen) with food in addition to paracetamol, provided no intolerance.  
  • Maintain adequate hydration and rest in a dark room as needed.
- Patient instructions:
  • Seek urgent medical review (call service or ED) if headache worsens, becomes sudden/severe, new neurological deficits, visual changes, vomiting, fever, neck stiffness, rash, or any airway/breathing difficulty develops.
  • Obtain home thermometer and monitor temperature.
  • Arrange blood pressure check (e.g., at local pharmacy or clinic) given OCP use and family history of hypertension.
- Follow-up:
  • Re-contact primary care if headache persists >48 h, recurs, or new triggers identified (e.g., menstrual cycle); consider formal migraine work-up or neurologic referral.
  • No additional ENT/allergy referral necessary at present as no airway/allergic features.

Quality checks:
● Missing but clinically expected elements: Objective neurological examination, fundoscopy, vitals (BP, HR, Temp), detailed medication doses/frequencies, documentation of any auto-injector possession (not indicated by history).  
● Conflicts between transcript and DDx: None noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear audio; minimal background noise; no inaudible segments affecting clinical content.
